A little bit about us.

We are the PDX Browncoats, the Portland Metro area Firefly/Serenity Fan Group and a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

With your help, we will repair and transport the Ariel Ambulance, from the Firefly episode Ariel, from Compton, California to Portland, Oregon so it can be part of GalactiCon 4 in Seattle. However, it is in disrepair and needs some TLC from the fan base. This is where you come in!
Time To Be A Big Damn Hero
By saving the Ariel Ambulance, we open up the opportunity for new fans, as well as seasoned veterans, to share in a piece of the Firefly world while helping socially responsible causes. 
As luck would have it, Ron Glass and Jewel Staite will be in attendance at GalactiCon. Obviously, we hope to reunite them with the iconic aircraft from the series.
With your help, we will repair and transport the Ariel Ambulance, from the Firefly episode Ariel, from Compton, California to Portland, Oregon. However, it is in disrepair and needs some TLC from the fan base. 
Once it is here in Portland, we will be marching with it in the PGE Starlight Parade in Portland, as well as having it on hand at CSTS. Later, it will make an appearance at GalactiCon 4 in Seattle.
Additionally, we are bringing film replicas for the original Battlestar Galactica from Colorado, and matching them up with replicas in Washington State to complete a 600 square foot display in the exhibit hall. 
Together, these will constitute a one-of-a-kind fan experience.
So Where’s My Gorram Money Going?
We need to fund the initial trailer repairs, new tires, safe transport and fuel. Once it is in Oregon, the Ariel Ambulance will need more extensive repairs like reattaching the tail, lighting and improvements for travelling to other events.
At the same time, we will be working to bring replicas from Colorado transported up to Seattle to be part of a larger display of film replicas for the original Battlestar Galactica.
Who Are You Again?
We are the PDX Browncoats, the Portland Metro area Firefly Serenity Fan Group and a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. We have integrated our shared appreciation for the stories of Joss Whedon into our social lives as well as our activism.

We raise money for charities with our annual Can’t Stop the Serenity Screenings and selling geeky & crafty merchandise at conventions in Oregon & Washington. We also volunteer at Oregon Public Broadcasting & the Oregon Food Bank.
PDX Browncoats provides volunteer assistance and financial contributions to nonprofits that promote equality for men and women, local action, and other ideals espoused in the works of Joss Whedon. We provide social outlets for fans of Whedon’s works because we have learned that socializing is an important step toward activism.
You can learn more about us at: pdxbrowncoats.com 
What's a "Browncoat"?
Browncoat is a slang term for a member of the Independent Faction, which lost to the Alliance in the Unification War, from the space western TV series ‘Firefly’ (and its big-screen sequel ‘Serenity’), created by Avengers Writer/Director Joss Whedon. It is also a nickname for fans who love the series.
Risks & Challenges
While our goal is small, and our team is mighty, we do have some risks and challenges with the campaign:
Without this campaign the Ariel Ambulance remain in a bit of disrepair. Some amazing Browncoats found her and brought her back to life, but it’s been some time since she’s had a proper showing. Without your support she’ll stay out of sight and continue to deteriorate. 
The biggest challenge is that if we miss our goal, even by a few dollars, we may not be able to do all of the work needed on her. This means we won’t be able to give the new, and current, Firefly fans the best possible experience.
And that's all there is to it.
Other Ways You Can Help
As our Big Damn Heroes said, "When you can't run, you crawl, and when you can't crawl - when you can't do that you find someone to carry you."
We need your help to boost the signal as far and wide as we can. Here are some ways you can help. 


Share, tweet, post, and help get this campaign out to all the Browncoats, and BSG lovers, you know. 


Tweet about the campaign with a message like

Be a Big Damn Hero and help the @pdxbrowncoats save the #ArielAmbulance http://igg.me/at/savethearielambulance


DON'T FORGET to use the share tools that Indiegogo has below our campaign video!! 
Our focus is to get the word to other fans out there. While you can reach our Big Damn Heroes on social media...we know their time is busy. Let's not bother them too much about the campaign and show them what we can do.
Remember...we are mighty!
